title: Probe handoff playground
content:
Context / intent:
This is a messy, personal scratchpad to capture a small set of prompt templates and few-shot micro-banks that I want to hand off to SRE/PromptOps for scaling and obfuscation tests. Not meant for production yet — just capture hypotheses, quick failing cases, and variant experiments.

Goals (fast):
- Surface brittle examples that blow up when context window shrinks or when we tokenize differently.
- Create a tiny canonical few-shot bank (~6 examples) for each pattern so others can reproduce.
- Note heuristics for fallback: when to truncate vs when to rephrase a shot.
- Quick checklist for converting to a stable template later.

High-level observations so far (intuition):
- Templates that use explicit numbered instructions (1/2/3) are more stable when we inject system-level role tokens, but more brittle to paraphrase.
- Short canonical examples reduce hallucination in the reranking stage; long-shot narratives sometimes override the instruction signal.
- Few-shot order matters much less than exemplar diversity for pragmatic tasks (summarization/bug triage); matters more for style transfer tasks.

EXPERIMENT BATCH A — instruction anchoring vs role-anchoring
Template A1 (instruction-anchored):
Prompt: "You are a developer assistant. Given the bug report below, produce a two-line summary and list potential root causes (3). Use terse bullets."
Shots (2):
- "Bug: app crashes on upload when file size > 5MB. Steps: attach, upload, crash.
  Summary: crash on large file uploads
  Causes: memory leak; improper chunking; file encoding mismatch"
- "Bug: login times out intermittently after SSO redirect.
  Summary: login timeout after redirect
  Causes: callback race; cookie domain mismatched; slow idp response"

Template A2 (role-anchored):
Prompt: "System: You are PRODUCT_TRIAGE_BOT v1. Respond as triage notes." (then examples)
Shots (2): same content above but with role marker.

Quick note: both produce similar quality on gpt-style models; on smaller open models role-anchoring reduced creative expansions (fewer invented causes). Keep this as a hypothesis.

EXPERIMENT BATCH B — few-shot set composition (diversity vs closeness)
Hypothesis: For stylistic imitation (customer-facing tone) few-shot should contain 4 same-domain examples (same product tone) + 2 cross-domain to inject variety.
Small set (6):
1) release-note blurb, formal
2) release-note blurb, casual
3) in-product tooltip, friendly
4) support email reply, empathetic
5) marketing microcopy, punchy
6) legal blurb, constrained (short)

Failure mode observed: when cross-domain shots are too dominant (3/3 split) the model flips to an inconsistent hybrid voice. So prefer 4:2 domain:outsider.

EDGE CASES / BRITTLE FAILS
- Tokenization boundary: examples where a critical number is split (e.g., v2.0.1 -> v2 .0.1) cause extraction heuristics to fail. Test with models using byte-level vs BPE tokenizers.
- Truncation ordering: When prompts are truncated from the front, anchored instructions at top are lost. So for low-window fallbacks, move critical instruction to the end with clear anchor token (===INSTRUCTION===).
- Repetition amplification: few-shot examples that repeat format markers ("Summary:") can cause the model to over-rely; sometimes it emits multiple repeated summary blocks. Consider single exemplar with multiple labels instead.

Quick reproducible test cases (copy/paste)
1) Summarization small-window test:
System: "You are a compact summarizer. Provide one-sentence summary.===INSTRUCTION===
Context: [insert long log repeated to exceed window]
Shots: (include 1 short example)
Expect: when truncated to 256 tokens, model should still produce a single short sentence. Failure: multiple sentences or omitted key phrase.

2) Extraction numeric edge:
Prompt: Extract the version numbers and file sizes.
Text: "Uploaded files: report_v2.0.1.pdf (size 12.5MB), snapshot_v10.4.tar.gz (size 20480KB)"
Expect: [v2.0.1, 12.5MB, v10.4, 20480KB]
Observed: tokenizers sometimes split v2.0.1 into tokens that the regex extractor missed. Test across our model catalog.

Conversion checklist for handoff (what I want PromptOps to do next):
- [ ] Convert these templates into JSONL examples + canonical evaluation harness (unit tests).
- [ ] Add sanitization step for version tokens (normalize v* patterns) before sending to small models.
- [ ] Run tokenization diff across supported models and note split cases.
- [ ] Try the ending-instruction fallback for low-window clients and compare accuracy.

Notes / chores (short):
- Slack thread: #promptops -> thread titled "probe-handoff: truncation anchor test" (ping Liam + Maya).
- Add experiment to RDW-4213 (linked).
- Save canonical few-shot banks under repo: github.com/redwood-inference/repro-playbooks (PR suggested above).

Random seeds / quick variants to try:
- Swap numbered list for bracketed labels [A] [B] — sometimes reduces hallucinated extra items.
- Replace explicit example labels ("Summary:") with in-band examples (one-line) to avoid label amplification.

Open questions / unknowns to capture:
- Does placing the instruction at the end always preserve instruction-following under LRU KV cache reuse? Probably model-dependent — need to test on our serving runtime cache settings.
- Is exemplar diversity better tuned by semantic distance or token-level distance? Create a small metric to quantify exemplar overlap.

End notes (meta):
This doc intentionally messy. If you take this on, please convert to a small repo folder with: 1) templates.md (cleaned), 2) tests/ (unit test cases), 3) tokenization-report.md, 4) conversion-checklist.md.
If anything confusing ping me (Asha) or drop a patch PR referencing JIRA-RDW-4213.

-----
Quick changelog: created 2025-10-03; edited 2025-11-08 to add numeric edge case example and handoff checklist.
